newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Bank Negara wins early battle against speculators.
newsitem.headline: Bank Negara wins early battle against speculators.

text.p: Malaysia's central bank on Wednesday appeared successful in its attempt to flush out ringgit speculators but the battle may have just begun, dealers and analysts said.
Bank Negara intervened aggressively late on Tuesday and again on Wednesday morning, selling large amounts of the dollar for ringgit.
The actual size of the intervention was not known, but dealers estimated that the central bank could have sold up to $1 billion. Bank Negara does not usually comment on its open market operations.
The intervention sent the dollar reeling from 2.5250 to 2.4950 ringgit, it lowest level since May 20.
At 0430 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5040/50 to a dollar.
"Bank Negara has won the first round, but this may only be the beginning," said Andy Tan, general manager at research house MMS International in Singapore.
The central bank has shown that it was not going to pull its punches, he said.
Some analysts said funds were expecting such an intervention and this might just be the prelude to a speculative attack on the ringgit after forcing Bank Negara to commit its reserve.
"After their recent victory over the Bank of Thailand, speculators are oozing with confidence and probably have additional funds to spare to stomach the initial sacrifice," one said.
In May, speculators unloaded the ringgit because of Thailand's financial crisis, forcing Bank Negara to intervene aggressively to stem the ringgit's losses.
The intervention saw the central bank's reserves fall by 1.4 billion ringgit ($560 million) at end-May. Bank Negara's reserves at the end of June stood at 70.71 billion ringgit.
But analysts said it would not be an easy task for speculators.
"The market will be foolhardy to take on Bank Negara," said Kobus Van der Wath, regional head of treasury economics at Standard Chartered Bank in Singapore.
"Bank Negara has shown its ability to maintain rates. They know how to handle such a situation and they will continue to be successful," he said.

Dealers and analysts said Tuesday's intervention was not unexpected as Bank Negara had defended the ringgit at the 2.5250 level for nearly two weeks. Before the intervention, offshore players out of London were seen testing the authorities after acquiring ringgit through swaps to run their long dollar/ringgit positions.
Analysts said it was likely the central bank, after squeezing speculators in the spot market, would come with another squeeze in the forward market.

This would force players who have borrowed ringgit at exorbitant levels to liquidate their positions, effectively flushing speculators with dollar/ringgit outright positions from the market, they said.
Analysts said that with uncertainty still clouding regional currencies, the ringgit would remain under speculative pressure.
"We may see another round," said Van der Wath.
Analysts expected dollar/ringgit to trade between 2.5000 and 2.5250 in the near term.
-- Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-201 4813)
